To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the addition of nanoparticles of cadmium sulfide to polyvinyl alcohol matrix leads to an improvement in polymer resistance to UV illumination.

1) The stability of polyvinyl alcohols to UV light is enhanced by introducing semiconductor nanoparticles into the polyvinyl alcohol matrix; 2) The stability enhancement is achieved by lowering the probability of photoactivated formation of defects within polyvinyl alcohol molecules.
the stability of the polymeric materials can be improved by incorporation of semiconductor nanostructures.

the development of new polymer nanocomposites for the protection of polymers and polymeric materials from the UV light damage.
development of polymer composites for UV protection.
the improvement of polymer endurance to photochemical degradation.

the UV protection is achieved via the reduction of the probability of polymer excitation and de-excitation via energy drain to the embedded nanoparticles.
the CdS nanoparticles embedded into the polyvinyl alcohol matrix are effective in protecting the polymer against photo-activated formation and accumulation of defects.
the UV stability of the polymeric matrix is enhanced by the incorporation of semiconductor nanoparticles.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the CdS nanoparticles are effective in the protection of polymeric materials from UV radiation.
the polymer protection is achieved by the introduction of semiconductor nanoparticles into the polymer.
the CdS nanoparticles can serve as efficient UV filters for the polymer matrices.
The main takeaway from our work is that
polymer protection against UV illumination is achievable by introducing semiconductor nanoparticles into polymeric matrix.
the polymer UV protection efficiency can be improved by a factor of up to 10, which is sufficient for many practical applications, including polymer-based solar cells.
the stability of polymer against UV degradation can be improved by the incorporation of semiconductor nanoparticles into the polymer matrix.
